sources.title: Naga Tourism: 2024 fluvial gathering
sources.note: Reports 1.5 million devotees and the concluding Pontifical Mass at the Basilica. The crowd layout and ninety-minute Mass duration are illustrative.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: updated 2026 fluvial schedule
sources.note: River conditions moved the 2026 departure to 21:00 with an estimated ninety minutes on the water. This annual replay instead uses an illustrative 16:00–18:00 window.

sources.title: City of Naga: 2022 fluvial procession and concluding Mass
sources.note: Documents the foot procession after the 14:00 Cathedral Mass and the concluding Mass; does not establish a 16:00 fluvial departure.

sources.title: OSM Basilica Loop and owner annotation
sources.note: OSM Basilica Loop outer curb; project owner annotated atlas image, 2026-10-07. Boundary follows the main loop and short north pieces, offset outward four metres from the mapped six-metre carriageway centreline.

sources.title: Daily Tribune: 2026 Traslación
sources.note: Reports both images reaching Porta Mariae around 18:30, followed by Holy Mass, with about 820,000 devotees. The number drawn is illustrative.

sources.title: Project owner: Cathedral precinct annotation
sources.note: Project owner annotated atlas image, 2026-10-07. Boundary fitted around the annotated forecourt and mapped east garden with a four-metre curb margin. Altar shifted four metres north within the annotation tolerance to clear the mapped overhead arch; placement is approximate, not a surveyed festival arrangement.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: 2026 festival calendar

sources.title: Naga Tourism: parade traffic advisory and official map
sources.note: Official 2026 map inspected: Panganiban Drive, south on Elias Angeles, west on Caceres, north on General Luna to the Plaza stage. Blue judging area faces the plaza.

sources.title: Philippine Information Agency: 72 contingents in 2023

sources.title: City of Naga: 2023 parade event window
